### Browser tools on chat sessions
> [!NOTE]
> Hosted browser availability depends on the account and deployment. The browser workspace must be enabled to open the live pane i
n the Playground.
`POST /chat-sessions/messages` accepts an optional `browser: { policy?, profileId? }`. Attach it on every turn that should browse.
The initial grant and profile are fixed; the current host policy and pinned read-only mode can narrow the effective permissions.
Responses and traces include the read-only `chatSessionId`, browser metadata, and screenshot URLs without inline image data.
| Method | Path | Purpose |
| POST | `/chat-sessions/browser` | Create an empty API session and its browser with `projectId`, `policy`, optional `profileId`,
and a stable `idempotencyKey`. |
| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/open` | Open or wake the session browser. |
| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/command` | Execute a browser command under the session policy with a stable `commandI
| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/note` | Append a command-ledger note. |
| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/trace` | Read command receipts and screenshot evidence. |
| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/artifact` | Resolve a command screenshot URL. |
| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/close` | Release the session desktop. |
Only the owning user can drive an API session's browser. All inputs use the public `sessionId`; conversation and browser identifie
rs in responses are informational. Capacity refusals before execution release the turn lease so the same idempotency key can be re
tried. An execution with an unknown outcome must be inspected before attempting a new action.

# Local Evals
> Run an MCPJam eval suite file on your machine with mcpjam test with local results and an MCPJam identity
> [!NOTE]
> The upcoming SDK 10, CLI 6, and Vitest 0.3 releases require an MCPJam login or `sk_` API key for every eval, including BYOK runs
with uploads disabled. These versions must ship after the backend run-start endpoint is deployed. Earlier versions keep their exi
sting behavior.
`mcpjam test <file>` runs an MCPJam suite file locally: it connects your MCP servers, drives each case's prompts through a model,
grades the transcript with the same assertions a hosted run uses, and decides the run with the same verdict policy. Bring your own
provider key and authenticate the run with MCPJam. With MCPJam-hosted inference it uses your existing CLI login and billing.
Results are **never uploaded**. The command writes results to your terminal and, if you ask, to a report file. It records the run
start with MCPJam. Like every command, it sends the CLI's single anonymous [telemetry](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/telemetry.md) e
vent, which `--no-telemetry` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` turns off; the run adds no telemetry of its own.
## Eval identity and local data
Run `mcpjam cloud login` locally, or set `MCPJAM_API_KEY` to an organization `sk_` key in CI. The SDK also accepts `apiKey` or `mc
pjamAuth` in run options. Explicit credentials take precedence over `MCPJAM_API_KEY`, which takes precedence over the saved CLI lo
gin. An invalid explicit credential never falls back to another account. CI never starts an interactive login. Ask an organization
admin for a key if you cannot create one.
Every logical run needs an online start response. MCPJam retries transient failures within ten seconds, then stops before executio
n. A prior successful run does not enable offline execution. The CLI resolves the project using its existing `--project`, environm
ent, and linked-project settings; a key can only access its own organization.
